answer.root_cause: In whence/interp.py's _compile_binop, the fast-path closure for '+' (f_add, which computes x + y) was guarded by `if op != '+':` instead of `if op == '+':`. This inverted condition made every non-'+' operator (notably '*', but also '-', '/', '%', comparisons) get compiled as addition instead of their real operator, while '+' itself fell through to later, unrelated branches.
answer.summary: Changed the guard on the addition fast-path closure in _compile_binop from `if op != '+':` to `if op == '+':`, restoring correct dispatch so '*' (and other operators) compile to their own semantics instead of being silently replaced by addition.

results.final_text:
`x + y`, so `x * x` silently computed `x + x`. This matched the observed hello.lang failure exactly (squares came out as `2x` instead of `x²`, and the resulting `total` of 30 instead of 55 made the `total > 50` check pick the wrong branch too).

The one-line fix (`!=` → `==`) restores correct dispatch for `*`, `-`, `/`, `%`, `==`, `!=`, and comparisons, since `+` now takes its own correctly-guarded branch and everything else falls through to its own `if op == ...` block as originally intended.
